text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Using renewable energy has improved my business.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Employees are happier in a sustainable workplace.’
How could you test this claim?
You should consider the types of information, sources of evidence or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Paolo’s statement. Explain why it is a prediction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Why might Adriana’s statement be biased?

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Paolo’s or Adriana’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to increase the use of renewable energy.
The following actions have been suggested:
• Promoting renewable energy through advertising.
• Building more renewable energy sources.
• Educating communities about climate change.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your recommendation
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
